title: Questionnaire orchestration playbook for customer security engagement
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a pragmatic, engineer-friendly guide for orchestrating responses to customer security questionnaires (vendor risk assessments), with a focus on RBAC v2, audit log schema, SIEM export mechanics, and evidence automation. Intended audience: security engineering, product security, solutions engineers, and CS reps who respond to or assemble artifacts for questionnaires.

Quick TL;DR (for on-call / rapid response):
- Use the "RBAC summary" template for questions about roles and least privilege.
- Point customers to our SIEM export sample (Elastic/Splunk) and include the JSON schema snippet under "audit_log_schema.json" (see linked artifacts).
- Attach automated evidence bundle from /evidence-exports when available; if not, run the ad-hoc script (see step 4).

Scope / When to use this doc:
- New inbound security questionnaires (SaaS integrations, enterprise trials)
- Periodic reassessments requested by customers
- Pre-sales technical due diligence calls that require written artifacts

Pre-engagement checklist (quick):
- Confirm questionnaire scope and deadline (reply within 48 hours to set expectations).
- Identify required artifacts: role matrix, audit log example, retention policy, SIEM export mapping, encryption/KMS statements, SOC/ISO attachments.
- Assign owner (security engineer) + reviewer (solutions eng or product lead).
- Check existing evidence exports: Confluence page "Trust Evidence Vault" and /evidence-exports for pre-generated bundles.

Templates and suggested language (copy/paste friendly):
- RBAC / Permissions: 
  "Redwood Inference implements RBAC v2: roles are scoped by tenant and environment. Roles are grouped into platform, infra, and customer-facing categories. Each role grants a narrow set of named permissions (read, write, manage, operator) and can be further scoped by resource attributes. We enforce least privilege and recommend customers use role bindings to limit access to production resources."
  Follow-up details to include: role naming convention, example role -> permission mapping, how service accounts are handled, and how timed access (EPHEMERAL tokens/OAuth) is implemented.

- Audit log summary: 
  "Every user-initiated and system-initiated action that affects customer data or control plane state is recorded in the audit log. Logs include timestamp (ISO8601), user_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip_address (when available), region, result (success/failure), and a free-text context field for additional metadata. Logs are retained according to contract: default 90 days for hosted; extendable for Dedicated/Private via config."

Audit log schema (concise field list for questionnaire answers):
- timestamp
- request_id
- user_id
- principal_type (user, service, system)
- actor_email (if applicable)
- action (verb)
- resource_type
- resource_id
- params_summary (truncated JSON string)
- outcome (success/failure)
- ip_address
- region
- trace_id
- prev_state_hash (when state-change)
- audit_version: "v2"

NOTE: keep this section short in customer-facing answers; attach the schema file for details.

SIEM export mechanics (overview to include in answers):
- We support push-based and pull-based export patterns. Customers commonly consume via:
  1) S3 export (daily/rolling) + built-in S3 connector for Elastic/Splunk
  2) Direct syslog/CEF forwarder for Dedicated/private deployments
  3) Kafka topic with Avro/JSON payloads for high-throughput customers
- Exports include compressed, gzipped newline-delimited JSON with the audit log schema above. We sign exports with an HMAC token and provide object-level metadata with start/end timestamps and a manifest.json.

Sample Splunk ingest blurb (for questionnaire mouthfuls):
  "We provide a Splunk-ready export: gzipped newline-delimited JSON. Fields are mapped to Splunk sourcetypes; recommended index-time extraction and timestamp parsing are documented in our Splunk onboarding guide (link in linked_artifacts)."

Evidence automation and reproducible bundles (how to deliver):
1) Check for pre-generated bundle in Trust Evidence Vault (link above). If present, confirm it matches request scope and attach.
2) If not present, run the Evidence Exporter (policy-exporter) playbook: 
   - git clone github.com/redwood-inference/policy-exporter
   - ./scripts/generate_evidence --project $CUSTOMER_ID --scope "rbac,audit,siem" --since YYYY-MM-DD --out ./out/$CUSTOMER_ID-evidence.zip
   - The script generates: role-matrix.csv, audit_sample.json (30 days), siem_export_manifest.json, retention_policy.txt, kms_artifacts.txt.
3) Sanitize: run ./scripts/sanitize_sensitive ./out/.. to remove debug tokens and ephemeral keys.
4) Sign bundle with tooling (internal: signbundle v0.9) and upload to secure share.

Practical guidance for red team / engineering reviewers:
- If a questionnaire requests raw logs for review, prefer providing a redacted sample snapshot (audit_sample.json) rather than full production exports. Document redaction rules: remove PII in params_summary and truncate object payloads > 2KB.
- For RBAC questions that ask for implementation details, provide architecture-level descriptions but avoid divulging low-level secrets or token formats.

Short Q&A snippets (for CS to paste into forms):
Q: "How do you enforce least privilege?"
A: "RBAC v2 enforces least privilege: roles are composed of atomic permissions and bound to principals via role bindings. We provide time-limited role elevation flows for critical operations. Operational controls (approval workflows) are configurable for Dedicated/Private customers."

Q: "Can you export logs to our SIEM?"
A: "Yes. We support S3/Kafka/syslog export options. We provide a signed, gzipped JSON export and an import guide for common SIEMs (Splunk/Elastic). For high-volume exports we recommend Kafka with Avro schema to preserve type-safety."

Known gaps / open questions (things to resolve before sending to critical customers):
- Exact retention SLA for some long-tail customers on hosted: need finance/legal sign-off for extended retention pricing. Ticket: JIRA-SEC-987.
- Example queries for customers who want SOC/Compliance runbooks (we have a stub, needs examples).
- Automated redaction heuristic sometimes removes too much context for debugging; need one test-case where we keep safe debugging fields.

Suggested artifacts to attach (order of priority):
1) role-matrix.csv (example)
2) audit_sample_30d.json (redacted)
3) siem_export_manifest.json + sample file links
4) retention_policy.txt (contractual language)
5) KMS and encryption statement PDF (internal standard artifact)
6) link to Trust Evidence Vault (Confluence)

Unresolved TODOs (owner / ETA):
- [Maya P] Draft retention pricing clause for >1 year (due 2024-12-05)
- [Priya D] Create two Splunk query examples for common alerts (due 2024-12-12)
- [Liam O] Validate evidence exporter redaction rules against customer sample (due 2025-01-02)

Meeting prep checklist (for pre-sales call):
- Bring RBAC diagram (roles vs resources).
- Have a 2-slide SIEM export flow (S3/Kafka/syslog).
- Confirm whether customer requires on-prem collection (Private) or can accept hosted export.

Notes to self / scribbles: 
- If a customer insists on direct DB access for audit logs -> escalate to security leadership. We never grant DB access; always provide exports.
- For Dedicated customers we can offer configurable syslog endpoints in VPC peering flow — coordinate with infra team.

Appendix: quick sample audit log record (redacted)

Last notes: keep answers short and attach the schema and sample artifacts rather than pasting long JSON into questionnaire forms. When in doubt, escalate to product-security for technical sign-off.

End of playbook.
